Kitchen Inspiration — The Locked Eleven

The final reference set. Tap the ones you love most — a gold ring means selected. Then hit “Show my picks” and send the list back to Stefan.

A
✓
House & Garden UK / Herringbone House
Cream painted in-frame perimeter + plaster chimney hood + book-matched marble-look slab carried full height, warmed by a dark oak island — Shaker bones, modern calm.
Source: houseandgarden.co.uk
B
✓
Architectural Digest — Leslie Murphy, Murphy Maude Interiors
Cream inset joinery with glazed uppers, one warm cream-travertine slab run as worktop AND full-height splashback, and a dark-stained wood island with chamfered turned legs — vero-08's structure exactly. The bell-shaped verdigris hood with riveted brass banding is the sculptural volume elite-03 and the Los Feliz pick both ask for.
Source: architecturaldigest.com
C
✓
ELLE Decor — Marianne Simon Design
A near-literal restatement of vero-08: alabaster inset cabinetry, a tapered painted chimney hood with a nickel strap, and Calacatta/Carrara run as one slab from worktop to ceiling behind the range, book-matched up to the hood. Polished nickel rather than brass is the one metal deviation; bobbin-turned stools and dark plank oak carry the warmth.
Source: elledecor.com
D
✓
Martin Moore — Woodland gated estate
Proves the register works with a dark stone: cream in-frame joinery and a tall white mantel hood flanked by paired ovens, with a black-and-gold veined marble slab as both splashback and surround. Emerald velvet stools are the single accent — the discipline elite-03 models.
Source: martinmoore.com
E
✓
LUXE Interiors + Design — kitchen by designer Carter Kay
The only candidate found that steps the register off plain white stone: the slab is a heavily veined marble from Bottega by Stones International whose mustard-gold movement is the source colour for the custom butter-yellow lower cabinets (cream uppers stay quiet, so the yellow reads as the single permitted accent). Full-height slab behind the range under a cream bell-shaped chimney hood; Emtek hardware. Note honestly: hardware is dark, not brass.
Source: luxesource.com
F
✓
House Beautiful — Texas family home by Sarah Stacey
Cream inset cabinetry to the ceiling, full-height white-marble slab behind a black French range, and a soft-shouldered black mantel hood pinstriped in brass — then a freestanding light-oak butcher table with a COPPER-clad base as the island, which is the warm counterpoint and the second metal at once. Brass pot rail hung with patinaed copper pans; brass cup pulls and bridge tap; dark herringbone oak floor.
Source: housebeautiful.com
G
✓
Atlanta Homes & Lifestyles — kitchen by Matthew Quinn, Design Galleria Kitchen and Bath Studio
The magazine's own caption names the fitting: a Gothic arched steel casement 'framed by articulating sconces from Galerie des Lampes' — brass swing-arm task lights mounted straight onto the stone, which is the single most studiable hardware move in this batch. Cream in-frame cabinets with vertical brass cup pulls and round knobs, continuous marble slab with no tile field anywhere, and an arched metal hood banded in brass top and bottom.
Source: atlantahomesmag.com
H
✓
Flower Magazine, 'The Designers' Guide to Kitchen Lighting' — kitchen by Lisa Frantz; lighting by Urban Electric; photograph by Marco Ricca
Flower's caption: Frantz 'used a bold brass light square fixture over the island that complements the range hood' (Urban Electric) — a designer deliberately rhyming the pendant's brass frame with the brass banding on the curved hood. Quiet painted inset joinery with brass cup pulls and vertical handles; Calacatta slab on counters and up the range wall with no tile. Honest caveat: the paint is a soft grey-blue rather than cream.
Source: flowermag.com
I
✓
House & Garden UK / Ledbury Studio
Cream painted fronts plus ribbed-glass wall cabinets, with Cristallo quartzite run across worktop, island and full-height splashback — one monolithic cool plane, warm neutral joinery.
Source: houseandgarden.co.uk
J
✓
Martin Moore
The cleanest demonstration of 'one monolithic cool plane': a single beige-grey quartzite slab runs as worktop AND full-height splashback behind floor-to-ceiling cream Shaker joinery, with a radiused island end in the same stone. Brass-and-frosted-glass linear pendant is the only metal gesture; an ornate plaster cornice with cartouche supplies the period volume. Nothing on the walls, nothing patterned.
Source: martinmoore.com
K
✓
House & Garden UK — Martha Mulholland, 1920s Spanish villa, Los Feliz, Los Angeles
Soft plaster with rounded arrises, an arched soffit over the corner cabinets and a sculptural plaster hood with a white-oak mantel band; book-matched Calacatta slab backsplash, white inset cabinets with black hinges, an oak butcher-block island with a basin carved into it, and a terracotta picket-tile floor. Top-lit by a skylight — the brightest Mediterranean kitchen here.
Source: houseandgarden.co.uk
